title: Methane on an Interstellar Comet
hook: A comet from another star system swept through ours — and the Webb telescope caught methane on it, the first time that molecule has been seen on a visitor from beyond.
key_points: JWST studied 3I/ATLAS, a comet that originated outside our solar system.
It found methane — reportedly the first direct detection on an interstellar visitor.
The comet also carries unusually high carbon dioxide, unlike most local comets.
Scientists think solar heat reached deep icy layers, releasing methane that was buried.
content_html: Every so often an object from another star system passes through our own, and 3I/ATLAS is one of those rare interstellar visitors. According to a ScienceDaily report, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope turned its instruments on the comet and found something striking: methane, in what scientists describe as the first direct detection of that molecule on a comet born beyond our solar system. The comet also carries unusually high levels of carbon dioxide, setting it apart from the comets that formed close to home.
extra_html: These chemical fingerprints are valuable because they're a sample of material from another planetary system, delivered to telescopes that can read it in detail. Researchers think the methane had been locked beneath the comet's surface and only escaped once the Sun's heat soaked deep enough to reach buried icy layers. Studying how an alien comet's ices respond to our Sun offers a rare, direct glimpse of the raw ingredients that go into building worlds around other stars.

flashcards.prompt: What made the methane detection on comet 3I/ATLAS notable?
flashcards.back_html: It was reportedly the first direct detection of methane on an interstellar comet — a visitor that formed around another star.

flashcards.prompt: Why did scientists think the methane only emerged when it did?

choices.text: Solar heating reached deeper icy layers where methane was buried
The methane was created by sunlight from scratch
The comet collided with a planet

flashcards.explanation_html: Researchers believe the methane was hidden beneath the surface and escaped once solar warming penetrated to deeper, icier layers.

flashcards.prompt: How does 3I/ATLAS's chemistry compare with typical solar-system comets?

choices.text: It has exceptionally high carbon dioxide, making it unusual
It is chemically identical to ordinary comets
It contains no ice at all

flashcards.explanation_html: The comet carries strikingly high levels of carbon dioxide, one of the signs that it formed around a different star.
